spark.takeaway: Redis delivers sub-millisecond latency via RAM-resident data structures and a single-threaded event loop—no mutex contention, provided you avoid O(N) blocking commands.
spark.summary: Master Redis's single-threaded event loop, core data structures, Lua atomicity, eviction policies, and high-availability patterns.
spark.byteSummary:
Master Redis's single-threaded event loop, core data structures, Lua atomicity, eviction policies, and high-availability patterns.

Redis multiplexes thousands of TCP connections via epoll/kqueue and executes commands sequentially on one main thread—making every single command atomic.

Production Redis mastery means choosing the right structure (Hash, ZSet, Stream), configuring eviction (allkeys-lru/lfu), and designing for sentinel/cluster failover.

domain.name: Redis
domain.description: Master Redis's single-threaded event loop, core data structures, Lua atomicity, eviction policies, and high-availability patterns.

learningJourney.title: Single-threaded event loop & memory-first design
learningJourney.explanation: Redis multiplexes thousands of TCP connections via epoll/kqueue and executes commands sequentially on one main thread—making every single command atomic.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
# Atomic Redis Lua sliding-window / token check (Python)
LUA_CHECK = """
local cur = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or '0')
if cur + tonumber(ARGV[1]) > tonumber(ARGV[2]) then return 0 end
redis.call('INCRBY', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[3])
return 1
"""
```
caveats: Never run `KEYS *` or huge `SMEMBERS` in production—O(N) commands stall the single main thread for all clients. Use `SCAN` instead.

learningJourney.title: Strings, Hashes, Sorted Sets & HyperLogLog
learningJourney.explanation: Choosing the right Redis type cuts memory usage and turns multi-round-trip client logic into O(log N) server operations.

tabbedExplorer.name: Sorted Set (ZSet)
tabbedExplorer.title: Skip List + Hash Table
tabbedExplorer.desc: Maintains unique members ordered by floating-point score in O(log N) for ZADD and ZRANGEBYSCORE.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Ideal for real-time leaderboards, delayed job queues, and exact sliding-window rate limiters.
tabbedExplorer.use: Top-K rankings, time-ordered feeds, rate limiting.

tabbedExplorer.name: Hash & HyperLogLog
tabbedExplorer.title: Compact Objects & Probabilistic Counting
tabbedExplorer.desc: Hashes pack small objects via listpack; HyperLogLog estimates unique cardinality up to billions in just 12 KB.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Use HyperLogLog (`PFADD`/`PFCOUNT`) when ~0.81% error is acceptable for unique visitor counts.
tabbedExplorer.use: User session fields, unique DAU counters.

learningJourney.title: RDB vs AOF, eviction policies & Redis Cluster
learningJourney.explanation: Configure `maxmemory` and an explicit eviction policy (`allkeys-lru` or `allkeys-lfu` for caches; `noeviction` for queues/locks).

learningJourney.title: Hot keys, cache stampede & big-key deletion
learningJourney.explanation: Protect Redis from memory exhaustion, thundering herds, and network saturation.

qaDetails.summary: Why does deleting a 500MB Hash with DEL freeze Redis, and what should you use instead?
qaDetails.body: `DEL` frees memory synchronously on the main thread. Use `UNLINK` so memory reclamation happens asynchronously on a background BIO thread.

qaDetails.summary: How do you mitigate a hot key receiving 200K reads/sec on one Redis shard?
qaDetails.body: Add a short-TTL L1 in-process cache (e.g., Caffeine) in app servers or replicate the hot key across N salted keys (`key#0..key#N`).

knowledgeCheck.question: Which Redis command reclaims a multi-million-element Hash without blocking the single-threaded event loop?

options.feedback: DEL frees memory synchronously on the main thread, stalling all clients.
Correct! UNLINK unlinks the key immediately and frees its allocations asynchronously on a background thread.
FLUSHDB wipes the entire database and blocks unless ASYNC is passed.

tipsAndTricks: Always set TTLs on cache keys and jitter expiration times (+/- 10%) to avoid synchronized cache stampedes.
Use `allkeys-lfu` for skewed workloads (Zipfian hot keys) and `noeviction` when Redis stores rate-limit/queue state.
In Redis Cluster, wrap related keys in `{user:42}:profile` and `{user:42}:cart` hash tags so multi-key Lua scripts land on the same hash slot.
domainContent.finalSummaryEyebrow: The idea to keep with you
domainContent.finalSummaryTitle: Keep keys bounded, run multi-step mutations in Lua, and never let cache stampedes hit your primary DB.
